title: Keel's most valuable operational powers are whitelists granted by Sky core contracts, revocable outside Keel governance
content:
Two On-chain Parameters record permissions Keel holds but does not own. A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.4.2: "the ALMProxy for Keel is whitelisted on the LitePSM. This allows Keel to call `buyGemNoFee` and `sellGemNoFee` on the `MCD_LITE_PSM_USDC_A` contract." A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.4.3: "Keel's SubProxy must be authorized by the Pause Proxy contract to send cross-chain messages on Solana."

Both are load-bearing. Fee-free access to Sky's Peg Stability Module is what makes moving between USDS and USDC costless enough for an allocation strategy to be profitable at scale, and Pause Proxy authorization is what lets an Ethereum-governed Agent act on Solana at all.

Neither privilege lives in Keel's Artifact as a right. They are entries in Sky's core contracts, granted by Sky governance, and removable by it without any Keel process being involved. So the real boundary of an Agent's autonomy is not the text of its Artifact but the set of whitelists Sky maintains — and revoking one is a faster, quieter remedy than any of the governance mechanisms elsewhere in the document.

Recording these dependencies as `[Core]` parameters is nonetheless the right call: it makes the Agent's reliance legible to its own tokenholders, who would otherwise have no way to see that Keel's business model rests on permissions it cannot defend.
description: The ALMProxy is whitelisted on the LitePSM for fee-free USDC conversion, and Keel's SubProxy must be authorized by the Pause Proxy to send cross-chain messages to Solana.
